metas.name: Canada - Bollard
metas.note: Alberta has a unique black and white bollard that is often found at intersections. It has a cylindrical shape and two black bands that wrap all the way around. It is one of the most useful Canadian bollards to learn because it appears so frequently.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec guardrail Bollards
metas.note: Quebec has unique bollards that are always attached to guardrails. They are long, thin white poles with a red or green reflector at the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Saskatchewan & Manitoba Bollard
metas.note:
Manitoba uses black and grey painted bollards. Most of the time an orange stripe will be present below the grey one.

  • Wooden, rectangular bollards of this form are typically found further north in Manitoba

NOTE: Bollards in this format with just a black top are seen in Manitoba and Saskatchewan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Chile - Bollards
metas.note: Chilean bollards are similar to Spanish style bollards, with a white reflector at the front and a yellow-orange reflector at the back. They are not super common. While regular bollards are somewhat rare in Chile, you may sometimes find this orange, temporary bollard, with two white stripes at the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Colombia - Spanish bollard
metas.note: This spanish bollard is mostly found in Cundinamarca, the area surrounding Bogotá, but also on the 40 towards Villavicencio.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Bollards
metas.note:
Ecuador is one of the few Latin American countries where bollards are very common.

You will find two main types of bollards:

  • A round bollard with two red stripes,

  • A flat bollard with two red reflectors on black.

Many other bollards can be found, however, they will almost always have the same colour scheme and style.

NOTE: A similar rectangular bollard can sometimes be found in Malaysia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Mexico - Bollard
metas.note: These small, cylindrical white bollards with a black base are unique to Mexico. A yellow reflector is sometimes seen, as well as a flat version.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Jalisco Bollard
metas.note: Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a crown and the text ‘Jalisco’ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Nayarit Bollard
metas.note: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Peru - Bollards
metas.note:
Bollards in Peru are painted red or yellow, and the country mainly uses a variety of triangularshaped concrete bollards. Occasionally you will also spot other designs, such as these circular concrete variants.

NOTE: These concrete variants can also be found in Bolivia and Brazil so do not rule out these countries if you find such bollards.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Lima/Ica 1S Bollard
metas.note: These bollards are only found on the 1S highway between the towns of Ica and Lima.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Moquegua Bollard
metas.note: This cylindrical bollard, with a black and yellow stripe at the top, is unique to the state of Moquegua, which is located in the south of Peru.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - North Lima Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is only found on the 1N highway north of Lima (still within Lima region).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Tacna Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is almost exclusive to Tacna region. It does spill into Moquegua but it is by far most common in Tacna.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Idaho/Utah Bollard
metas.note: This thin bollard with a small white reflector at the top is unique to Utah and Idaho
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Montana/South Dakota Bollard
metas.note:
The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.

NOTE: These bollards can be found to a lesser extent in other western states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Nevada Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Oregon Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is unique to Oregon state in US.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Washington Bollard
metas.note: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Western Bollards
metas.note:
These bollards are found in the upper western states from Utah to Washington.

  • The white version is more common in Washington, Oregon and Idaho

  • The green version is more common in Montana, Idaho and Utah

  • The black version is more common in Wyoming, Utah, South Dakota and colorado

NOTE: Technically, all colors can be found in every western state, but the likelihood of finding them is higher in the states listed.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Wyoming Bollard
metas.note: Roadside bollards in Wyoming often feature a dark metal pole with a white circular reflector at the top. The top of the metal pole is sometimes painted white or grey, which is unique to Wyoming
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: Uruguay - Bollard
metas.note: These white bollards, with one side often painted yellow, and stone barriers, are specific to Uruguay.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.
